html:
MatAnyone (Yang et al., S-Lab NTU, CVPR 2025): video matting of one object: from a mask of the object in the first frame it tracks the object and outputs a soft alpha matte (hair, motion blur) for every frame, with a memory of earlier frames. Non-commercial code and weights (S-Lab License 1.0).

Commercial use: no (code: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); weights: LicenseRef-noncommercial).

Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/pq-yang/MatAnyone at e5ddc534c1ff
  • Code licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/pq-yang/MatAnyone/blob/e5ddc534c1fff9bb9e54cf476095d29071b7cb4f/LICENSE ; https://github.com/pq-yang/MatAnyone/blob/e5ddc534c1fff9bb9e54cf476095d29071b7cb4f/README.md (weights: https://github.com/pq-yang/MatAnyone/releases/tag/v1.0.0)
  • Training data: VM800 (MatAnyone video matting foregrounds), Composition-1k (Adobe Deep Image Matting), Distinctions-646 (image matting), BG-20k (background images), DVM background set (video backgrounds), COCO 2017 (train, instance annotations), YouTube-VIS 2021 (video instance segmentation), Supervisely Person Dataset (human segmentation) (doc/TRAIN.md: matting on VM800 (not released) and ImageMatte (Distinctions-646 + Adobe Image Matting), backgrounds from BG-20k and DVM, segmentation on COCO, YouTube-VIS 2021 and Supervisely Person.)
  • Options: warmup = 10 (>= 0; also n_warmup), dilate = 10 (>= 0; also r_dilate), erode = 10 (>= 0; also r_erode)
  • Kernel libraries: image_normalize
  • Variants: matanyone
  • Outputs: alpha
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): matanyone 3000x4000 (14.5 GiB peak allocated, 15.1 reserved)
  • matanyone 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 36 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • matanyone 100x288x512, first call: TensorRT fp32 16 s (ONNX + engine).
  • matanyone original 1080x1920: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); pq-yang/MatAnyone@e5ddc534c1ff process_video loop on frames in memory, cv2 mask closing
  • matanyone portable 1080x1920: Portable reuses frame-zero encoder features during warm-up. Synthetic output and all 300 alpha maps from three labeled YouTubeMatte clips matched bitwise.
  • matanyone kernels 1080x1920: Eager CUDA decoder reuses activation storage after projecting the residual.
  • matanyone portable 100x288x512: The archived portable run used the same 100 YouTubeMatte frames, initial mask and FP32 settings as the staged TensorRT run.
  • matanyone load / first call: original 3.39 s / 2.37 s, portable 0.4 s / 1.867 s, kernels 0.35 s / 1.559 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Video matting, YouTubeMatte (MatAnyone's benchmark): each clip at 512 x 288 with the authors' first-frame mask, the authors' evaluation settings (1 warm-up step, mask closing 4 px); 8-bit alpha against the ground truth: mean absolute and squared difference and the temporal coherence error dtSSD (lower is better), averaged over frames, then clips. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1e-06 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 8.3e-05 and p99 <= 0.0001 (absolute error of the output alpha).

Limitations

  • torch.compile compiles the image encoder, mask encoder and tensor decoder. It runs the recurrent memory and video loop eagerly. Each new input shape has a compilation cost.
